name: Terbutaline

card.summary: A prescription beta-2 agonist for asthma with an FDA boxed warning against use in preterm labour; no appearance trials exist.
card.note: Boxed warning: oral terbutaline not approved for tocolysis; serious maternal heart events and deaths reported.

quick.overview:
Terbutaline is a beta-2 adrenergic agonist bronchodilator used as a reliever for asthma and reversible airway disease. It is available as tablets and injection and, outside the US, as an inhaler.
It appears in appearance discussion only as a member of the beta-2 agonist family. Its use for fat loss or muscle is not documented, and no trials exist for that purpose.
quick.mechanism: It selectively stimulates beta-2 receptors, raising cAMP and relaxing bronchial smooth muscle. Wikipedia reports an elimination half-life of 11 to 16 hours and notes it is less susceptible to metabolism by COMT than catecholamines.
quick.risks: The label lists nervousness, tremor, headache, palpitations and tachycardia, and carries a boxed warning against use for preterm labour after maternal deaths and serious cardiac events. It is prescription-only, and WADA prohibits it except inhaled with a prior therapeutic use exemption.

lead: Terbutaline is a prescription selective beta-2 adrenergic agonist sold as Bricanyl, Brethine and Marex, among other names. In bodybuilding and fat-loss circles it is discussed as a stimulant-type fat-loss and pre-workout aid in the same family as albuterol (salbutamol) and clenbuterol: users describe it as a way to feel energised and, through beta-2 stimulation, to nudge metabolic rate upward while dieting toward a leaner look.[8][10]

Medically it was patented in 1966, entered use in 1970 and is indicated for preventing and reversing bronchospasm in people aged 12 and older with asthma, bronchitis and emphysema.[3][4] It has also been used off-label to delay preterm labour, which led the FDA in 2011 to add a boxed warning on injectable and oral forms.[3][4]

Human studies of terbutaline concern asthma, COPD, and obstetric and other medical uses. A small body of infusion research on beta-2 agonists in lean men, quoted in forum threads, reports modest rises in energy expenditure, but no trial has tested terbutaline as a fat-loss or muscle-gain agent.[10][11]
infobox: Prescription-only; WADA-prohibited except inhaled with TUE[4]

paras: Terbutaline is a reliever for asthma and bronchospasm; inhaled forms work within about 15 minutes. [3][4] Several classic asthma trials used it as the comparison beta-2 agonist against inhaled budesonide. [1][2]
Off-label, it has been used as a tocolytic to delay preterm labour for up to 48 hours. [4]

On T Nation, users who compare beta-2 agonists describe terbutaline as an option next to albuterol and clenbuterol for fat loss. One poster said it felt strong compared with albuterol, 'like short acting clen or more'; another said they liked albuterol or terbutaline with caffeine before training for energy, adding that these 'don't raise blood pressure much' for them.[8][9] A thread on a two-week fast cites a statement that beta-2 agonists including terbutaline could help limit muscle loss when combined with exercise.[12] These are user reports and anecdotes, not trial results.

The US label lists effects similar to other sympathomimetic amines; the Grokipedia summary of the label gives nervousness, tremor, headache, palpitations and tachycardia as the most common. [3][5] Wikipedia lists tachycardia, anxiety, tremor, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia and rarely pulmonary edema. [4]

In February 2011 the FDA required a boxed warning that injectable terbutaline should not be used for preterm labour beyond 48 to 72 hours and oral terbutaline not at all, citing serious maternal heart problems and death. [3][4]
Its tertiary butyl group increases beta-2 selectivity, and it lacks the 4-hydroxy group that makes catecholamines susceptible to COMT. About 90% is excreted in urine. [4]

Grokipedia's summary of the label says oral effects start within roughly 30 to 120 minutes and last up to about 8 hours, with inhaled forms acting faster.[5] Wikipedia gives an elimination half-life of 11 to 16 hours and says about 90% is excreted in urine.[4] A pharmacology paper described its elimination pathways.[13]
The World Anti-Doping Agency prohibits terbutaline like all beta-2 agonists, except when inhaled with a therapeutic use exemption obtained in advance. [4]

Wikipedia gives 1966 as the patent year and 1970 as the start of medical use [4]. Grokipedia says the FDA approved terbutaline on March 25, 1974 [5]. The 2011 FDA safety action against prolonged tocolytic use followed reports that Grokipedia counts as 16 maternal deaths between 1976 and 2009 [5]. In bodybuilding writing from the 2000s, terbutaline appears in threads about clenbuterol and albuterol as a less common beta-2 option [8][10].

sections.h: Reported risks in off-label physique use
paras: The common effects in the label summary, nervousness (reported in up to about a third of patients in Grokipedia's account of the label), tremor, headache, palpitations and tachycardia, are the same ones that forum users mention when describing stimulant-like beta-2 agonists [3][5][9]. The label cautions about cardiovascular disorders, diabetes, hyperthyroidism and low potassium, since the drug can worsen tachycardia, arrhythmia or high blood sugar [3][5]. Sports bodies treat the class as prohibited, with the exception of inhaled use under a therapeutic use exemption [4].
No clinical trial has tested terbutaline for fat loss or muscle gain. Published and registered trials concern respiratory and obstetric uses.

In asthma, a randomized blinded comparison enrolled 103 patients with newly detected asthma and compared inhaled budesonide with inhaled terbutaline over long-term treatment; the 1991 report concluded the corticosteroid was more effective than the beta-2 agonist, and a follow-up trial examined reducing or stopping budesonide and crossing patients over from terbutaline.[1][2] In a 52-week double-blind trial, adults and adolescents with mild asthma used as-needed terbutaline alone, as-needed budesonide-formoterol, or twice-daily budesonide plus terbutaline as needed; terbutaline served as the reliever comparator.[14] The PRACTICAL trial, a 52-week open-label study in New Zealand adults aged 18 to 75, compared budesonide-formoterol reliever therapy with maintenance budesonide plus as-needed terbutaline.[15]

Registered trials include a phase 3 study of 250 people comparing a beta-2 agonist with ipratropium plus beta-2 agonist in COPD exacerbations, a pilot safety study in 9 children with type 1 diabetes, and an acute tocolysis study of 100 women with suspected fetal distress.[6][7][16]

Related work on beta-2 agonist metabolism is quoted on forums: direct infusion of salbutamol and terbutaline in lean men produced a modest increase in whole-body energy expenditure, according to a passage reproduced in several T Nation threads.[10]

timeline.event: FDA requires a boxed warning against preterm-labour use. [4]

lore.intro: Terbutaline appears in T Nation threads about beta-2 agonist fat burners as a less common relative of clenbuterol and albuterol, often discussed alongside stimulants and caffeine.[8][9][10]

claims.claim: Terbutaline works like a short-acting clenbuterol for fat loss.
claims.believers: One user who tried it reported it felt stronger than albuterol, 'like short acting clen or more', and others describe beta-2 agonists as part of a cutting toolkit.[9]
claims.experts: Beta-2 agonists raise energy expenditure modestly in infusion studies of lean men, per a passage cited in forums; no trial has measured fat loss with terbutaline, and the label lists tremor, palpitations and tachycardia among common effects.[10][3]

claims.claim: Beta-2 agonists help preserve muscle while dieting or fasting.
claims.believers: A poster in a fasting thread said a beta-2 agonist such as terbutaline could help limit muscle loss with exercise.[12]
claims.experts: Published terbutaline trials address airway disease and obstetrics; none examine muscle retention during fasting.[1][14]

claims.claim: Terbutaline plus caffeine gives pre-workout energy with little blood-pressure effect.
claims.believers: One user said the combination made them feel 'wired' and did not raise blood pressure much.[8]
claims.experts: The prescribing information lists nervousness, tremor, headache, palpitations and tachycardia as common reactions to terbutaline and cautions about cardiovascular disease.[3]

angle.text: Physique forum users who mention terbutaline use it, or describe using it, as a shorter-acting alternative to clenbuterol or albuterol for energy and fat loss, sometimes alongside caffeine before training. The appearance effect is a claim built on beta-2 pharmacology; trials of terbutaline itself address airway disease.
